Peptide was dissolved in PBS to prepare a 1 mg/mL stock solution and then gradually diluted into different concentrations (0.5 mg /mL, 0.25 mg/mL, 0.125 mg/mL, etc.). Fluorescamine powder was dissolved in DMSO to prepare a 3 mg/mL working reagent. In a 384-well black plate, 27 μL of peptide solutions at different concentrations were mixed with 9 μL of fluorescamine working reagent. After incubating for 15 min in the dark, the fluorescence intensity (excitation wavelength at 395 nm and emission wavelength at 470 nm) was recorded by a microplate reader. A standard curve was obtained based on the concentration of the peptide solution and its corresponding fluorescence intensity.
Male Kunming mice (weighing 20 ± 2 g, 6–8 weeks old) were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 3 mice per group) and intravenously injected with peptide (5 mg/kg, 100 μL). At 2, 6, 12, and 24 h, the organs were collected and homogenized in PBS. After centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 10 min, the supernatant was collected. In a 384-well black plate, the supernatants (27 μL) were mixed with the fluorescamine working reagent (9 μL, 3 mg/mL) and incubated in the dark for 15 min. The fluorescence intensity was tested by a microplate reader using the excitation wavelength at 395 nm and the emission wavelength at 470 nm. The amount of peptide at different time points was calculated using a standard curve (Supplementary Fig. 3l). Additionally, peptide was marked by FITC and the distribution of fluorescence was then observed by a small animal live imaging system (Bio-Rad ChemiDoc MP, Times-Legend Bioscientific Co., LTD) at 6 h after intravenous injection with FITC-peptide, respectively. Finally, the mice were humanely executed and the organs were ex vivo imaged immediately after in vivo imaging at 6 h.

bacteria_induced_pneumonia_model: The in vivo antimicrobial activity of the peptide was assessed by the pneumonia model. Male Kunming mice (weighing 20 ± 2 g, 6–8 weeks old) were induced neutropenia by injection i.p. with two doses of cyclophosphamide on day 1 (150 mg/kg) and day 4 (100 mg/kg). On day 5, mice were i.p. administered pentobarbital at a dose of 60 mg/kg and infected by injecting MRSA ATCC 33591 (25 μL, 1 × 109 CFU/mL) or K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603 (25 μL, 1 × 109 CFU/mL) via intratracheal spraying. Mice were randomly assigned to four groups (6 per group). They were injected i.p. with peptide or vancomycin (for MRSA ATCC 33591 infection) or polymyxin B (for K. pneumoniae ATCC 700603 infection) at a single dose of 5 or 10 mg/kg at 4 h, 8 h and 12 h post-infection, respectively. The model group was injected with the same volume of normal saline. After 24 h post-infection, the mice were euthanized, and the lung was taken out for bacterial counting and histopathological examination.
reverse_transcription_quantitative_real_: RAW 264.7 cells were cultured in DMEM medium containing 10% FBS and seeded in a 12-well plate with a cell density of 1 × 105 cells/well for 24 h at 37 °C in 5% CO2, then exposed to LPS from E. coli O111: B4 (1 μg/mL) for 1 h. Following incubation with peptide solutions for 2 h, total RNA of RAW 264.7 cells was isolated and analyzed. Total RNA was extracted with TRNzol isolation reagent (TIANGEN, China) and reverse-transcribed to cDNA using a high-capacity reverse transcription kit. The target mRNA amount in the samples was detected using SYBR-Green, and the relative mRNA expression levels of various genes were determined by quantitative RT-qPCR on the QuantStudio 3 Instrument (Applied Biosystems, USA). Normalized to the mRNA expression level of β-actin, the mRNA expression of other genes was calculated using the 2−ΔΔCt method. All primers used in this study were designed for this project using the NCBI Primer-BLAST tool and were synthesized by Sangon Biotech (Shanghai, China). The paired primers used for amplification are listed in Supplementary Table 1.

On day 5, mice were i.p. administered pentobarbital at a dose of 60 mg/kg and modeled by injecting LPS from E. coli O111: B4 (5 mg/kg) via intratracheal spraying. Mice were randomly assigned into three groups (6 per group) and injected i.p. with the peptide at a single dose of 5 mg/kg at 2, 6 and 10 h post molding, respectively. The model group was injected with the same volume of saline. After 12 h post molding, the mice were euthanized and the lung was taken out for extracting total RNA to analyze by RT-qPCR and for histopathological examination.
in_vivo_toxicity_assay: The in vivo toxicity of the peptide was tested by a single intraperitoneal injection in mice. Specifically, Kunming mice (weighing 20 ± 2 g, 6–8 weeks old, randomly allocated 4 male mice and 4 female mice to each group) were i.p. injected with the peptide or polymyxin B at a single dose of 20, 30 or 40 mg/kg. Saline was employed as the control group. Behavior, weight and survival of mice were recorded for 7 days or until death. Additionally, mice were sacrificed after 7 days post administration, serum and urine were collected for biochemical and protein expression analysis, and organs were harvested for histopathological examination and transcriptome analysis. Renal tubular injury score was estimated in renal tissue stained with hematoxylin and eosin70. Renal tubular injury is classified into six levels based on brush border loss, tubular dilation, cast formation, tubular necrosis, and neutrophil filtration. Ten high-power fields were chosen randomly, with scores ranging from 0 to 5 for each field (0: normal; 1: mild injury, affected 0–10%; 2: moderate injury, affected 11–25%; 3: severe injury, affected 26–49%; 4: highly severe injury, affected 50–75%; 5: extensive injury, affected 75%). All evaluations were conducted by two researchers who had no knowledge of the experimental conditions.
enzyme_linked_immunosorbent_assay_elisa: The ELISA kits used to detect the levels of mouse neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL) (JX-3003A1, Yancheng Junxing Biotechnology Co., Ltd, China), Cystatin C (JX-3175A1, Yancheng Junxing Biotechnology Co., Ltd, China) and kidney injury molecule-1 (Kim-1) (JX-3054A1, Yancheng Junxing Biotechnology Co., Ltd, China) in serum and urine. The operations were conducted according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
biodistribution: Male Kunming mice (weighing 20 ± 2 g, 6–8 weeks old) were randomly assigned to four groups (n = 3 mice per group) and intravenously injected with peptide (5 mg/kg, 100 μL). At 2, 6, 12, and 24 h, the organs were collected and homogenized in PBS. After centrifugation at 10,000 × g for 10 min, the supernatant was collected. In a 384-well black plate, the supernatants (27 μL) were mixed with the fluorescamine working reagent (9 μL, 3 mg/mL) and incubated in the dark for 15 min. The fluorescence intensity was tested by a microplate reader using the excitation wavelength at 395 nm and the emission wavelength at 470 nm. The amount of peptide at different time points was calculated using a standard curve (Supplementary Fig. 3l). Additionally, peptide was marked by FITC and the distribution of fluorescence was then observed by a small animal live imaging system (Bio-Rad ChemiDoc MP, Times-Legend Bioscientific Co., LTD) at 6 h after intravenous injection with FITC-peptide, respectively. Finally, the mice were humanely executed and the organs were ex vivo imaged immediately after in vivo imaging at 6 h.
standard_curve_of_fluorescamine_assay: Peptide was dissolved in PBS to prepare a 1 mg/mL stock solution and then gradually diluted into different concentrations (0.5 mg /mL, 0.25 mg/mL, 0.125 mg/mL, etc.). Fluorescamine powder was dissolved in DMSO to prepare a 3 mg/mL working reagent. In a 384-well black plate, 27 μL of peptide solutions at different concentrations were mixed with 9 μL of fluorescamine working reagent. After incubating for 15 min in the dark, the fluorescence intensity (excitation wavelength at 395 nm and emission wavelength at 470 nm) was recorded by a microplate reader. A standard curve was obtained based on the concentration of the peptide solution and its corresponding fluorescence intensity.
statistical_analyses: Data normality was tested by the Shapiro-Wilk test and graphically by QQ plot (R). Data were expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD) and statistically analyzed by GraphPad Prism version 9.0 (Chicago, IL, USA). Student’s t test (two-tailed) was used to determine significance between the two groups. Exact p values are shown on the graph.
